text:
Mia: seeing a slow memory creep in KV on a few hosts after long-context loads. not a spike, just a steady +20-80MB/hour on a 48GB card
Arjun: hmmm. which workload? chat history or long-form generation?
Mia: long-form with repeat-prefixes + heavy attention windows (seq len ~12k intermittently). multi-tenant box with 6 active tenants.
Sam: any pprof or heap dump? could be fragmentation vs actual resident growth
Mia: grabbed a quick pmap + /proc/pid/smaps snapshot. pmap shows anon RSS trending up, smaps shows many small anonymous mappings. dumping pprof now (cpu/alloc).
Arjun: also check KV pagewalk stats and kernel pagemap churn. I remember a similar symptom when kernels flipped for large page vs small page alignment.
Mia: attaching quick snippets inline:
```
# top lines
PID   RSS
1234  12.1G
# pmap tail
00007f... rw-p  8K
00007f... rw-p 16K
... many small mappings
```
Sam: small mappings could be our slab allocator splitting pages. if fragments aren't reused, resident increments over time. do we compact after evict?
Mia: eviction rate steady, but reuse score for pages created by longctx tenants is ~0.02 compared to 0.6 for shortctx tenants. means pages created during long contexts rarely get reused.
Lin: that smells like a reuse fingerprint mismatch. longctx requests allocate large KV segments that aren't referenced again because prefix caching bypasses for those requests.
Arjun: could be interaction with batching heuristics too — we changed batching window to 25ms last month, might increase concurrent unique prefixes -> fragmentation up
Sam: good point. we can try two quick experiments: 1) force smaller batching window for a tenant synthetic workload 2) run a reclaim pass that aggressively coalesces adjacent free pages after eviction
Mia: I have a repro harness: run 6 tenants, each does 30k tokens with periodic prefix shifts. script: tools/kv-sim/longcreep.sh (invokes loadgen --seq 12k --rotate-prefix).
InfraBot: deploy pipeline: ci/kv-repro/3502468000 started by Mia. logs at https://ci.internal/3502468000
Arjun: also profile kernel selection path — when we pick largepage vs smallpage kernel the malloc alignment changes. need to log kernel choice per allocation.
Mia: added extra logging to runtime: TRACE kernel_pick=%s alloc_size=%d tenant=%s. rolling to staging now.
Sam: for immediate mitigation, do per-tenant soft watermarks: lower watermarks for longctx-heavy tenants so they get evicted earlier and don't leak. but that may cause regressions for latency-sensitive tenants.
Lin: propose a smoothing quota curve: when a tenant's residency slope > threshold over window, throttle their allocation rate (soft throttle) rather than immediate eviction. avoids oscillation.
Arjun: yes — a leaky-bucket style quota with exponential smoothing. implement in allocator: track EWMA of residency delta and cap new allocations if EWMA > X.
Mia: I'll implement a quick prototype behind feature flag and run the repro for 12h. will report pmap + reuse scores.
Sam: also add a background defrag compaction that merges adjacent free slabs every 5min; cheap if we limit to slabs < 1MB.
Mia: noted. I'll run two branches: (A) smoothing+throttle (B) periodic compaction.
Lin: remember to test with mixed tenant weights — one noisy tenant at 60% throughput and five at 8% each to catch isolation issues.
Arjun: and capture kernel vmstat counters: page_faults, majflt, compaction_failures.
Mia: pushing results to the ticket: https://redwood.internal/issue/KV-3502 . will update by EOD tomorrow with numbers.
Sam: awesome. if you need help writing the perf harness I can pair.
Mia: thanks — pulling Sam in now.
InfraBot: CI/kv-repro/3502468000 finished: 3 failed, 12 passed. artifacts: https://ci.internal/3502468000/artifacts
Mia: follow-up: staging run with smoothing flag reduced slope by 72% and reuse score rose to 0.34 from 0.02. still monitoring for latency regressions.
Arjun: great signal. next steps: instrument kernel_pick, land smoothing as opt-in, and add compaction as optional background job.
Lin: also add tenant-level telemetry in console: residency slope graph + EWMA threshold alerts. product asked for that.
Mia: agree. filing small PRs for telemetry and the feature flag. will coordinate rollout plan. :thumbsup:
